edits.description: Caps how many unprompted texts each parent gets in a day, stops non-urgent ones outside allowed hours and labels each one so you know which job sent it. A text stopped by the cap or the hours is dropped, not sent later, so scheduled jobs are timed inside the allowed hours in the first place. caveats: Each iPhone can already silence the night on a schedule, so what Happy adds is the daily cap, the urgent or not-urgent split, the label and the pause by chat.

Scheduled jobs are therefore timed inside the allowed hours, and the hook is the backstop.

It is not a hard gate for scheduled texts: the message_sending hook that sees `--announce` deliveries lets the message through if the plugin throws or times out, and only the agent's own message tool is gated fail-closed.

demand_source.supports: A shipping family assistant sells the same function: it reads school emails and newsletters and sends parents a daily digest of what to know, do and decide.

edits.description: A separate mailbox registered with school, PTA, coaches and the lunch system is read by an isolated, memory-less reader, so no parent's private inbox is touched. Weekday afternoons both parents get a five-line text of the day's school and activity mail with dates spelled out, a dated to-do list, and one line per child from the school platforms' own summary emails where the school uses them. A parent who wants a day-before reminder for a line asks their own agent for it.
edits.example: Trigger: weekdays at 16:00. Text: 'School mail today: picture day is Thursday 15 October, order form due Wednesday 14 October; PTA meeting moved to Tuesday 20 October at 7 pm; lunch balance is low.' Jordan then texts Happy: 'remind me Tuesday evening about the picture day form.'
caveats: Pick the mailbox provider with the password in mind: the plugin signs in with a mailbox password only, which on Gmail means a Google app password that Google does not recommend, while OpenClaw's guide names Fastmail and iCloud.

Each school system has to accept an extra guardian address, a manual chore per system, and auto-forwarding from a parent's Gmail may fail the plugin's aligned-DMARC check, so registering the address directly is the safe route.
The reader gets body text and attachment file names only, so PDF or image newsletters and flyer attachments are not read.

Urgent alerts are not this digest's job, since the school's own alerts reach the parents' phones first; the reader keeps one backup rule (a closure, delay or early-dismissal message from an allowlisted school sender is passed on at the next sweep, not held until 16:00), and sorting urgent from routine on real district mail is untested.

PowerSchool emails carry grades and attendance and Classroom summaries carry assignment titles: these are a child's education records and they reach the cloud model under store:false, which is why the card is rated medium risk.
Classroom summaries (missing and upcoming work, no grades) arrive only if the school uses Classroom and the teacher switches them on, and the guardian invitation expires after 120 days.
One job appears to take one delivery target, so two parents need two jobs or the parents' group chat, and the iCloud read path likely needs an in-house himalaya wrapper.

For a school or team app that sends no email, try the app's own email notifications into this mailbox first and a parent's screenshot to Happy second; Canvas and ClassDojo have no verified email path.

The reminder step is not wired end to end. The reader that writes the digest holds no reminder or store tool, on purpose, because it reads untrusted mail, and it is untested whether the parent's own agent, which receives any reply, can see the digest text. Until that is tested, a parent names the line when asking their own agent for a reminder. Giving the reader a write to the household store would let text from a school email reach the parents' private agents, so that route needs its own review first.
unverified: Whether the district, PTA, coaches and lunch system each accept an extra or shared guardian address; this is a manual chore per system.

Auto-forwarding school mail from a parent's Gmail by filter may fail the plugin's aligned-DMARC check (Google's forwarding guidance says forwarded mail often fails SPF); DKIM survival was not tested, so registering the address directly is the safe route.
An iCloud+ custom-domain address with this plugin was not tested; Apple documents the IMAP host and app-specific passwords, not this combination.

Whether himalaya has an MCP mode; its README does not mention one, so the iCloud path likely needs an in-house wrapper. The README also says native keyring support was removed in v2, so its password comes from a command.

decision: whether personal mail may be read by the cloud model with storage off (the roadmap's M4 rule is a local model only, and no local model is installed)
llm-task plugin enabled in config
caveats: The roadmap's M4 keeps each inbox on a local model so that mail never leaves the Mac. There is no local model today, so this digest would send personal mail to the cloud model; whether that is acceptable under store:false is Tony's open decision, and the digest waits on it.

Google announced a Gmail 'AI Inbox' in January 2026, described as like a personalised briefing that highlights to-dos, for trusted testers first with wider release promised later. If it has reached the parents' accounts it covers much of this digest inside Gmail, so check before building.
Reply drafts are left out: the roadmap treats them as optional ('if ever added'), and Gmail's own conversation summaries, Help Me Write and Suggested Replies are free for all users.

Google's Gemini app lists "Daily digests of your calendar, to-do list, and emails" among its scheduled actions for personal Google accounts (being rolled out gradually, up to ten active actions). That digest is prepared inside Google, where the mail already lives, so try it on one parent's account before building this.

demand_source.title: Ohai: Your Household Manager for Calendars, To-Dos, Emails & Family Life
demand_source.supports: A shipping family assistant scans emails, PDFs, photos and documents for important dates and deadlines and suggests calendar events and alerts from them.

edits.example: Jordan sends a photo of the soccer season schedule. Happy replies with the eight game dates it read, each spelled out in full, flags one with no start time, and asks whether to set a reminder the evening before each. Nothing is written until she answers.
edits.how: Prompt-level standing order on top of F002 and F007 (F010 for calendar); plain conversational proposal rather than ask_user, whose wait is 900 seconds by default and which the docs say is not for confirming a plan. Optional extraction step: the bundled llm-task plugin returns the dates as a schema-checked list (enable the plugin, add it with tools.alsoAllow, pass a JSON schema, list both custom model ids in llm.allowedCompletionModels, keep allowModelOverride false).
depends_on: F002 photo and PDF reading with inbound attachments on
F007 reminders
F010 calendar create, for the calendar half only
F031 household store, only for keeping dated rows such as a lunch menu
caveats: For one event on a poster, a recent iPhone can already do this by itself: pointing the camera's Visual Intelligence at something with a date on it offers to add the event to the calendar (the iPhone 16 family, per MacRumors' guide to the feature). Happy's part is what that does not cover: a sheet with many dates, a PDF, a day-before reminder, and the calendar or list both parents share.
Dates read from a photo can be wrong (a missing year, two children on one sheet, a blurry corner), so every proposal spells each date out in full and nothing is written until the parent says yes.
The calendar half waits on calendar create (F010); until then the offer is reminders only.
A monthly lunch menu or a season schedule is one more dated document: the proposed rows are stored (F031) only after a yes, and Happy is never the allergy authority.
unverified: Date extraction accuracy on real flyers (missing years, two children, blurry photos) has not been measured.
End-to-end behaviour of the calendar half was not assessed because it waits on F010; the reminder half needs only F002 and F007.

Which iPhones the parents carry: MacRumors' guide lists Visual Intelligence for the iPhone 16 family. Apple's own iPhone guide page for the feature returned only its menu in this review, so the phone-side claim rests on MacRumors and iPhone Life.
Whether llm-task runs with a truly empty tool surface on Happy's OpenAI provider route; the doc says the Agents API runtime may keep built-in helpers.
